kernels.term: Plate tectonics as an Earth-system model

definition.text: Plate tectonics is the model that connects moving lithospheric plates with the origins of continents, oceans, mountains, earthquakes, volcanoes, and continental drift.

anchor.quote: Plate tectonics is the model or theory

facts.text: The model explains features including folded rocks, mountain ranges, earthquakes, volcanoes, and continental drift.

anchor.quote: folded rocks and mountain ranges, of earthquakes and volcanoes, and of continental drift

facts.text: Earth's lithosphere consists of the crust and rigid outermost mantle and is divided into moving tectonic plates.

anchor.quote: The crust and outermost rigid mantle together make up the lithosphere.

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 1.5, BCcampus Open Education

definition.text: Rigid lithospheric plates move above mantle rock that remains solid yet can flow slowly, while heat transfer sustains mantle convection.

anchor.quote: solid rock, but is plastic enough to be able to flow slowly

facts.text: Upward mantle flow at ocean ridges helps form new lithosphere while plates diverge.

anchor.quote: new lithosphere forms (at ocean ridges), and the plates move apart

facts.text: At convergent boundaries, one plate can be subducted into the mantle beneath another.

anchor.quote: one plate will be subducted (pushed down) into the mantle beneath the other

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 1.5, BCcampus Open Education

definition.text: Plate boundaries are classified as divergent, convergent, or transform according to whether plates separate, approach, or slide alongside one another.

anchor.quote: The three types of plate boundaries are divergent, convergent, and transform

facts.text: Divergent boundaries move apart and form new crust, whereas convergent boundaries move together and can subduct crust.

anchor.quote: divergent (plates moving apart and new crust forming), convergent (plates moving together and one being subducted)

facts.text: Transform boundaries accommodate plates moving side by side rather than creating or subducting crust.

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), chapter 10 summary, BCcampus Open Education

definition.text: Volcanic magma forms chiefly at divergent boundaries, convergent boundaries, and mantle plumes through decompression or flux melting.

anchor.quote: magma is formed at three main plate-tectonic settings

facts.text: Divergent boundaries and mantle plumes generate magma by decompression melting, while convergent boundaries use flux melting.

anchor.quote: divergent boundaries (decompression melting), convergent boundaries (flux melting), and mantle plumes (decompression melting)

facts.text: At a spreading ridge, upward-moving mantle begins partial melting because pressure decreases near the surface.

anchor.quote: partial melting starts because of decompression

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 4.1, BCcampus Open Education

definition.text: The rock cycle describes the continuing transformation of crustal materials and is driven by Earth's internal heat engine and the solar-powered hydrological cycle.

anchor.quote: constantly being changed from one form to another

facts.text: Earth's internal heat moves material through the core and mantle and contributes to changes within the crust.

anchor.quote: Earth’s internal heat engine, which moves material around in the core and the mantle

facts.text: The hydrological cycle moves water, ice, and air at the surface and is powered by the Sun.

anchor.quote: the movement of water, ice, and air at the surface, and is powered by the sun

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 3.1, BCcampus Open Education

definition.text: Relative dating orders geological events by interpreting relationships such as superposition, inclusions, and cross-cutting without assigning numerical ages.

anchor.quote: look at the relationships between them

facts.text: In an undisturbed sedimentary sequence, superposition places older layers below younger layers.

anchor.quote: the layers at the bottom are older than those at the top

facts.text: A feature that cuts across or disrupts another geological feature must be younger than the feature it disrupts.

anchor.quote: must be younger than the feature that is disrupted

attribution: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 8.2, BCcampus Open Education
